title: City of Sequim v. Malkasian
questions: The City wishes to test the validity of an initiative that was adopted as a city ordinance by 78% of the voters. Did the City sue the correct party when it sued an individual citizen who had been a member of the organization that sponsored the initiative, and if it sued the wrong party, should that citizen recover his attorney fees for defending the ordinance?

title: Alby v. Banc One Financial
questions: Susan Alby sold property to her niece. The deed transferring the property contained a clause providing that ownership of the property would return to Alby if the property was mortgaged or encumbered during Alby’s lifetime. Was this clause an unlawful restraint on alienation of property and therefore invalid?

title: State of Washington v. Gregory
questions: Eugene Allen Gregory was convicted of three counts of first degree rape for the rape of one woman. He was then convicted of aggravated first degree murder for the rape, robbery, and murder of another woman. For the murder, Gregory received a sentence of death. Gregory now appeals the conviction and sentence in each case.
